study: CPI Rent OER Lodging first-vintage category numeric forecasting with training-only expanding-window Ridge and fixed baselines
unit: MAE pp of MoM seasonal-adjusted first-release ALFRED indices
conclusion: RESEARCH ONLY: OER and Rent ridge forecasts show lower holdout MAE than a 3-month mean across seven 2026 months, but still make large misses. Lodging prior-year seasonal same-month forecast has lower holdout MAE than three-month mean, while pre-2026 sample shows opposite ranking. No robust statistically established gain.
releaseUse: Not promoted into CPI or Core CPI live engine. Components alone cannot substantiate all-items CPI accuracy.
limitations: Seven 2026 holdout cases too few for reliable deployment or near 100% accuracy claims
Some category regressors re-estimate on earlier release results; no future outcomes entered predictions
The 26-case sample excludes 2026-10 for pre-release category history gap, not imputed
CPI rent/OER/lodging are seasonally adjusted index-derived first vintages, not necessarily exact rounded official BLS press numbers
Need recent inflation regime stability and more independent out-of-sample 2027 releases before claiming predictive skill
Lodging new prior-year seasonal model was not best in 2024-2025; its 2026 result may not generalize
